issues.cell: law 1 (11)'s 'fixed by an earlier step of its event' (PRB7G-GEN-02, PRB7G-TIM-03) x law 2 (c)'s unwalled stage ('no Enceinte or Gate recorded ... no harbour gate ... a castle welded to it re-sited by F-CASTLE else kept inside') x the check's (11) record ('the stage plan S3 (6)-(9) fixed') and exceptions ('its target, its edit, the run its own law re-traces')
issues.claim: Since pass 7 law 1 (11) holds every Tier-1 thing from the step that fixes it: S3 (7)'s main gates, harbour gate and a carried way's gate and S3 (8)'s weld vertices, town-side gate and vertex towers are held before S3 (9) traces. When the pull and F-WALL's raised-way rung find no lawful stage-1 trace round a standing raised way, law 2 (c) leaves stage 1 unwalled at S3 (9): every such gate removed and the welded castle re-sited (its fixed places moved whole) or kept inside (its weld vertices gone) - a removal and a move 'by a meeting', so law 1 (11) is false at the stage end (no lawful outcome), unless the rung's removal is read as the op's own law (its save clause names hand and epoch removals; a castle re-site is no edit of the trace op's). The check splits likewise: its exceptions name no law 2 (c) stage, a generation names no target, and 'the stage plan S3 (6)-(9) fixed' read after S3 (9) passes while each fixing step's record (S3 (7)'s gates, S3 (8)'s welds) fails E_INVARIANT on law 2 (c)'s own outcome. Re-siting a castle's held fixed places for a meeting moves Tier 1 (J148's tier text) on the program's reading. Same class at a village's F-V-RAISED (time lens).
issues.required_change: Law 1 (11): '(a run deleted, buried, converted or dismantled; the run a moved vertex or a water op re-traces between the towers its own law leaves unaffected)' -> '(a run its op deletes, buries, converts or dismantles; the run a moved vertex or a water op re-traces between the towers its own law leaves unaffected; a stage law 2 (c) leaves unwalled, with the gates fixed for it and a castle welded to it)'; the check: '(11)'s exceptions read from the event (its target, its edit, the run its own law re-traces)' -> '(11)'s exceptions read from the event (its target, its edit, the run its own law re-traces, a stage law 2 (c) left unwalled)' (+14 words, payable by merging law 2 (c)'s list into 'none of its wall's records'). Alternative keeping the castle: law 2 (c)'s 'a castle welded to it re-sited by F-CASTLE else kept inside' -> 'a castle welded to it kept on its claim, its outer arc its own curtain, its town-side gate and vertex towers where S3 (8) fixed them', the weld vertices leaving with the wall by the exception.

issues.cell: law 1 (10)'s merged lead 'no op makes or deepens (commit) a meeting with a shape-held thing:' x its list (no line across a vault-use span of it, no aqueduct merged into it, no soffit lowered over a run of it, no gate made in it) x *meeting* ('any contact') x correction 6 ('every list an example gives of lawful crossings, impassables ... reading so') x veto 23 x E-P1, E-P9 x J147 (3), J149's reading, J149 applied clause 8
issues.claim: Pass 7 merged pass 6's 'a shape-held thing takes nothing newly from a meeting' into 'no op makes or deepens a meeting with a shape-held thing', followed by a list of meetings that change the locked thing. At a regeneration or a rebuild under a shape lock: S6's aqueduct crossing a kept shape-locked ring over (nothing of the ring written), a re-derived ring passing beneath a kept shape-locked road deck's open span (the cap the ring's own reading), a castle claim, S3 (7) gate or S7 tower under a shape-locked aqueduct's clearing arch - each a meeting made newly, none changing the locked thing. Reading A (the lead, which correction 6 extends to every example's list of crossings and impassables): all barred - the aqueduct not built (it cannot bend round a closed ring to its basin), the ring to F-WALL's rung else unwalled, no claim, gate or tower there. Reading B (the list, as (10)'s own 'a thing held in shape its shape', pass 6, J147 (3) 'the shape-locked wall never changes', J149's 'the aqueduct passes over it', J149 applied clause 8, E-P1 and E-P9 read it): all lawful. Two aqueducts, rings and castles; §5.3's row reading (10) by the meetings made newly fails B's build under A; T110-4's shape-locked runs carry the split on every path. Reading A narrows J149's reading. No case turns on undo, redo, a re-grade or a repair (J150).
issues.required_change: Law 1 (10): 'and no op makes or deepens (commit) a meeting with a shape-held thing: no wall-like line, ...' -> 'and no meeting an op makes or deepens (commit) changes a shape-held thing: no wall-like line, ...' (same word count); correction 6: 'no op makes or deepens a meeting with a shape-locked side (law 1 (10); J150)' -> 'no meeting an op makes or deepens changes a shape-locked side (law 1 (10); J150)'; veto 23: 'no op makes or deepens a meeting with a thing whose shape the user locked' -> 'no meeting an op makes or deepens changes a thing whose shape the user locked'. (If every meeting is meant: law 1 (10) '...: no meeting at all - an aqueduct over it and a wall beneath it among them -', E-P1 and E-P9 conformed, and the narrowing of J149's reading flagged for the owner.)

issues.cell: law 2 (a)'s pass-7 split 'an op whose event sets the line, point or value it changes ... takes the lawful shape law 3 picks nearest it, and every other (a pull or cost field, a route solve, a siting, a points-form drawWall's trace) searches only shapes law 1 admits, its own cost choosing among them' (PRB7G-LCK-06) x law 3's scope x *Not yet built*'s S7 towers x PRB7F-GEN-04 x *over the band*, *Strips, zones and nearest points*, E-P11 x §4.8 Towers, §4.4 S5a Trace (2)
issues.claim: Pass 7 turned (a)'s two closed lists into a dichotomy: what an event sets takes law 3; 'every other' op searches by its own cost. S7's spacing and turn towers and S5a's pins are set by no event and placed by a rule with no cost. On a valley-site CITY a stage ring passing beneath an S4 viaduct, or under S6's aqueduct whose arch clears the wall but not a tower, gets a spacing or turn tower in the strip (law 1 (5)); at stage k a pin's gatehouse meets another raised way's strip. Builder A (PRB7F-GEN-04's closure, the examples, E-P11, law 3's scope): that one tower to the nearest clear point either way, the rest unmoved; the pin to the nearest clear point on its arterial. Builder B ((a) as written): S7 'searches' by its own law - its spacing re-run over the lawful stretch, every later tower shifted, a turn tower (placed only at its turn vertex) not laid; the pull's cost picks the pin anywhere lawful in its band. Two tower sets, gates and traces on a common path; §5.3's row passes both, T110-4's same-seed digests split; the same reaches a harbour-mouth chain's heads and S3 (7)'s carried-way gate. PRB7F-GEN-04's closure fails in part: its mechanism, law 3, no longer governs the tower.
issues.required_change: Law 2 (a): 'and every other (a pull or cost field, a route solve, a siting, a points-form drawWall's trace) searches only shapes law 1 admits, its own cost choosing among them' -> 'and every other searches only shapes law 1 admits - a pull or cost field, a route solve, a siting or a points-form drawWall's trace by its own cost; a thing a step places by a rule with no cost (a tower by spacing or at a turn, a pin on its way, a chain's heads) by law 3, nearest the place its rule gives' (+18 words; *Not yet built*'s 'at a turn vertex or by spacing' may read 'by its rule', -4).

issues.cell: *Carried way*'s stage gate (PRB7G-GEN-01): its lead 'its gate at the first point beyond the foot' x 'taking its gate where that stage's boundary crosses its ground course or ends (... at a stage k >= 2 a pin of S5a, one of S5b's c), none where the boundary crosses only its deck' x the re-route when 'its gate law gives the way no lawful gate there' x the pull (S3 (9), S5a, S5d's top-up) x S5b's c and N_k x R7-03 (b), E-P9, E-P15, E-S3 x F-WALL's detection and ladder x §5.3's way-and-trace row
issues.claim: Pass 7 replaced the forced pick (which made a kept or prefix raised road's carried way one of S3 (5)'s routes, pinned, counted and gated) with a rule read on the boundary, while the way is met by the pulled trace and the count. For a drawn, unlocked raised road of class secondary over a valley outside the town: (i) where - the lead says the first point beyond the foot, the stage clause the boundary's crossing, E-P15 both; with T = t_1 crossing the ground course 200 m past the foot the gate is on the boundary (pinned by S3 (9)) or 170 m outside it beyond the pull's band (F-WALL's raised-way rung, else stage 1 unwalled); (ii) whether the trace keeps it - where the boundary crosses only the deck near a stair end, R7-03 (b) keeps an arterial's deck crossing beneath its deck but nothing keeps a non-arterial carried way's (E-P9 omits its ground course; law 1 bars no ground-way crossing): the pull (or S5d's top-up) keeps it beneath the deck, or crosses the ground course where no stage gate law is left to gate it - §5.3's way-and-trace row fails or F-WALL's last rung cuts the drawn way; (iii) when it counts - at stage k it is one of S5b's c, counted before S5a's pin finds it unlawful (a closing arc, a strip) and the way is re-routed through the nearest gate: N_k - 1 gates (F-WALL adding a postern) or, the gate law read before S5b counts, one more spawned primary and N_k gates, though the re-route's 'nearest gate' is unknown until S5b has spawned. Gates, traces, N_k and T110-4 (c)'s round-trip digest differ by builder.
issues.required_change: *Carried way*: 'its gate at the first point beyond the foot:' -> 'its gate where the wall crosses its ground course, never nearer the foot than the first point beyond it:'; '(... at a stage k >= 2 a pin of S5a, one of S5b's c), none where the boundary crosses only its deck (law 1 (3); ...)' -> '(... at a stage k >= 2 a pin of S5a, one of S5b's c only where its gate law gives it a lawful gate there, read before S5b counts - else re-routed at the trace step), none where the boundary crosses only its deck, the trace keeping each crossing as the boundary had it, at its gate or beneath its deck - its ground course beyond each foot impassable to the pull, as an arterial's is (law 1 (3); ...)'; E-P15's 'where T = t_1 crosses its ground course or ends, at the first point beyond its foot' -> '..., never nearer its foot than the first point beyond it'; E-P9's list adds 'a carried way's ground course beyond each foot where the stage's boundary crossed only its deck'.

issues.cell: *Carried way*'s stage-1 gate 'beside N1 as the harbour gate is' x *meeting* (the wall's moat; the way the raised way carries) x law 2 (a) (the moat by its own derivation), (b) (the carried way re-routed), law 1 (11) x S3 (10)'s decks 'at every main gate and at a harbour gate (7)' x S3 (11)'s serving gates and count x S5a Outer moats ('every way is kept with a deck') x §5.3's water row x E-P15, E-D18
issues.claim: On a walled CITY with a wet city moat (blueprint moat inner or all, a source within moat.waterReachM), Rebuild around my drawings or a regeneration keeps a drawn raised road whose carried way enters: S3 (7) gives it a gate on T = t_1 beside N1; S3 (10) carves the moat across the carried way (an L1 way standing since the prefix or kept). The moat and the carried way meet, and law 2 must resolve it: (a) lays the moat by S3 (10), which decks only main gates and a harbour gate - the way crosses water off a deck (§5.3's 'a way crosses water only on a deck' fails; the L0 batch cuts a finer edge at no prepared vertex): no lawful build; a builder reading 'as the harbour gate is' decks it; another takes (b), re-routing the Tier-3 way through a main gate's deck and leaving its own gate (Tier 1, held from S3 (7)) standing with no way, a postern by §2.7's Gate. Three outcomes for one crossing; at stage k S5a's outer moat decks 'every way', the pin among them, so stage 1 and stage k differ by reading. S3 (11)'s serving gates and its 'stay N, plus a harbour gate' count are restatements E-P15 left unconformed.
issues.required_change: *Carried way*: '(at stage 1 S3 (7)'s once S3 (6) has fixed the boundary, a gate beside N1 as the harbour gate is; ...)' -> '(at stage 1 S3 (7)'s once S3 (6) has fixed the boundary, a gate beside N1 and, as the harbour gate is, a gate of the stage to every rule that reads its gates - S3 (10)'s moat deck on a wet stretch, S3 (11)'s serving gates; ...)'; E-P15 adds S3 (10)'s 'with one deck at every main gate and at a harbour gate (7)' -> 'with one deck at every main gate, at a harbour gate (7) and at the gate a carried way standing before the stage takes (§2.7's laws, law 2 Carried way)' and S3 (11)'s 'stay N, plus a harbour gate of (7) where one was placed' -> '..., and the gate a carried way standing before the stage takes'.

issues.cell: E-P11 (§4.4 S5a Trace (2)'s pin: '... else that crossing takes F-WALL's raised-way rung') and E-D11 (F-WALL's detection cell; §5.4's W_RAISED_MEETING list) x *Carried way*'s order (law 2 (b) re-route, 'else the op takes law 2 (c)')
issues.claim: At a stage k >= 2 a carried way's gate is a pin of S5a; *Carried way* orders its unlawful gate (b) then (c) - the way re-routed through the nearest gate a way of its class may pass, else law 2 (c). E-P11, the text the pipeline seat writes at the pin, sends it straight to F-WALL's raised-way rung, skipping the re-route; and where the re-route fails, E-D11's detection names no carried way, so the rung its law 2 (c) needs is not detected and §5.4 lists no warning for it. The laws govern; the examples differ.
